rulings.challenge_claim: 16:10 carries the identical melekh root that anchors the following 16:12-16:15 kings run, undisclosed by the row's rejected_alternative/device_notes, which frame the 16:10-16:11 mishpat pair as sharing no catchword with that run.
rulings.grounds: byte tier + skeleton-tier sweep, independently re-derived (not trusting either packet's digit). sweep.py --skel מלך (final-kaf spelling) returns 24 verses book-wide including Prov.16.10, Prov.16.14, Prov.16.15; sweep.py --skel מלכ (medial-kaf plural/construct spelling) returns 10 verses including Prov.16.12, Prov.16.13 (plus the unrelated Prov.16.32 lakad-root false hit, correctly unclaimed by any row) -- the allography split OL's packet documents. Direct byte read of verse_map_oshb.json confirms the token forms: מֶ֑לֶךְ (Prov.16.10), מְ֭לָכִים (Prov.16.12), מְ֭לָכִים (Prov.16.13), מֶ֥לֶךְ (Prov.16.14), מֶ֥לֶךְ (Prov.16.15); the root is wholly ABSENT from Prov.16.11 (no מלכ skeleton substring anywhere in that verse's bytes). This confirms LF's re-derivation: a one-verse gap at 16:11 sits between two royal-noun occurrences, present at 16:10 and again at 16:12-16:15. P07-039's own device_notes states the pair 'sits immediately before the melekh/melakhim run of 16:12-16:15 without sharing that run's specific catchword' -- this is a byte-false claim: Prov.16.10, inside this very row's own span, contains מֶ֑לֶךְ, the identical root anchoring 16:12-16:15.
rulings.remedy: Rival-engagement rewrite (prose-only; NOT a respan -- the 16:10-16:11 span is byte-sustained and correct; any proposal to redraw either boundary is a boss-only proposal). Replace the false 'without sharing that run's specific catchword' claim in device_notes with an explicit disclosure that Prov.16.10 carries the identical royal-noun root anchoring the following run, then state the actual ground for keeping 16:10 with 16:11 rather than the kings run: 16:10 is bound to 16:11 by the shared mishpat root present in BOTH verses, while the melekh/melakhim run at 16:12-16:15 requires the royal-noun root in every verse of an unbroken span and 16:11 breaks that continuity -- so 16:10's mishpat tie forward is the row's chosen, stronger organizing principle, and its incidental royal-noun overlap with the following run does not itself warrant redrawing either boundary. Pair with the companion fix on P07-040 as one coordinated seam-pair edit (both rows sit on either side of the same 16:10 seam). Test the cure must pass (the test that killed the original): re-collate device_notes/rejected_alternative against sweep.py --skel melekh/melakhim output -- no non-overlap assertion may survive where the sweep shows overlap.

rulings.challenge_claim: The rejected_alternative misstates why the wider six-verse span was cut, blaming only 16:11's absence of the royal noun while lumping 16:10 into the same rejected span even though 16:10 independently carries the identical token.
rulings.grounds: Same underlying byte evidence as the P07-039 ruling above (melekh present at Prov.16.10, absent at Prov.16.11, present Prov.16.12-16.15) confirms the root-recurrence fact LF cites is true. But direct read of P07-040's actual rejected_alternative text does not lump 16:10 in as deficient: it reads 'A wider six-verse kings run proposed for 16:10-16:15 was tested and cut back: 16:11 carries zero instances of the melekh/melakhim root, so it is drafted with 16:10 as its own mishpat-linked pair instead' -- this explicitly carves 16:10 OUT into its own row and attributes the cut specifically to 16:11's absence, not to any claimed absence at 16:10. The row makes no false statement; LF's 'misstates ... lumping 16:10 into the rejected span' framing overstates what the text actually says. REFINE: the underlying defect is real and is the SAME cross-seam disclosure gap as P07-039 (the row never affirmatively states that 16:10 itself carries the identical royal-noun root), but the correct framing is under-disclosure, not misstatement. A secondary, narrower gap found on independent re-check: boundary_evidence_refs carries oshb: citations for Prov.16.12-16.15 but only web: (no oshb:) for Prov.16.10 and Prov.16.11, even though the rejected_alternative makes a Hebrew-root-absence claim specifically about 16:11.
rulings.remedy: Same coordinated seam-pair rewrite as P07-039's remedy (one edit spanning both rows). Add a sentence to this row's rejected_alternative disclosing that Prov.16.10 independently carries מֶ֑לֶךְ, the identical royal-noun root, and that 16:10's exclusion from this row is not because the root is absent there but because 16:10 is engaged elsewhere (the mishpat pairing with 16:11 in P07-039). Add oshb:Prov.16.10 and oshb:Prov.16.11 to boundary_evidence_refs to support the Hebrew-root-absence claim already made about 16:11. NOT a respan -- the 16:12-16:15 span is byte-sustained and correct. Test the cure must pass: check_refs_mirror.py confirms an oshb: citation for every verse argued in prose; re-collation against sweep.py output confirms no unsupported non-overlap assertion remains.

rulings.challenge_claim: The ish-opening construction run at 16:27-16:29 correctly breaks at 16:30's grammar, but 16:30 recycles the same rare tahpukhot noun used inside the cluster at 16:28, an undisclosed echo straddling the row's own right seam.
rulings.grounds: Independently re-derived: sweep.py --skel תהפכ returns 9 verses book-wide (Prov.2.12, 2.14, 6.14, 8.13, 10.31, 10.32, 16.28, 16.30, 23.33), confirming LF's digit for this rare root. Direct byte read of verse_map_oshb.json confirms the token תַּ֭הְפֻּכוֹת at Prov.16.28 (the vice-noun completing the row's own ish-construct template) and תַּהְפֻּכ֑וֹת at Prov.16.30 (object of 'devising') -- the identical root recurring one verse past the row's stated right boundary (16:27-16:29). The row's rejected_alternative and observed_substrate_signals disclose only the grammatical ish-opening template break at 16:30 ('16:30 breaks the run by opening with a participle... rather than ish') and never mention the shared vice-noun; the rationale's 'broken cleanly at 16:30' framing therefore overstates the seam's cleanliness for a rare, byte-true root recurrence the toolkit's cross-seam-cohesion rule requires disclosing. UPHOLD at medium: the grammatical (ish-opening) boundary genuinely holds and the span is not wrong, but the row omits a mandated disclosure of a byte-true device straddling its own seam.
rulings.remedy: Disclosure-only cure (NOT a respan), matching the pattern this same row already applies successfully to its own x-small-nun and ketiv/qere disclosures, and that P07-048/P07-055 apply to their own non-adjacent echoes. Add a sentence to observed_substrate_signals or device_notes stating that the tahpukhot vice-noun completing the row's own 16:28 clause recurs at 16:30 immediately outside the row's span (sweep.py --skel tahpukhot: 9/915 verses book-wide, a rare root), disclosed as texture rather than adopted as a boundary driver, since the ish-opening grammatical template that actually drives the row's cohesion argument genuinely stops at 16:29. Test the cure must pass: cross-seam check confirms every byte-true device touching the row's own boundary verses (16:26 before, 16:30 after) is named in the row, matching the standard already met by this row's other two disclosures.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's sole ground for the 16:8 boundary -- that the verse carries no form of the divine name -- is a Hebrew-token claim advanced with no quoted Hebrew and no oshb: citation anywhere in the row.
rulings.grounds: Confirmed on independent read: boundary_evidence_refs lists only web: refs (web:Prov.16.8, web:Prov.15.16, web:Prov.15.33, web:Prov.16.1 through web:Prov.16.9) -- zero oshb: entries; the divine-name-absence claim is stated in English only in rationale and observed_substrate_signals. Direct byte read of verse_map_oshb.json Prov.16.8 (טוֹב מְ֭עַט בִּצְדָקָ֑ה מֵרֹ֥ב תְּ֝בוּא֗וֹת בְּלֹ֣א מִשְׁפָּֽט) independently confirms the underlying claim is TRUE: no divine-name token, bare or prefixed, occurs in the verse -- so the boundary itself is correct; only the citation form is deficient. This is a genuine violation of the binding standing rule 'Quote the original language for every boundary-relevant original-language claim' (book_strategy Prov.md Sec.8 and TOOLKIT.md, both verbatim and mandatory). UPHOLD at low: no verdict or span change, citation-format defect only.
rulings.remedy: Add oshb:Prov.16.8 to boundary_evidence_refs; splice the byte-tier Hebrew of 16:8 into rationale or observed_substrate_signals alongside the existing English gloss (spliced from verse_map_oshb.json, never hand-typed). Test the cure must pass: citation_sweep.py / check_refs_mirror.py confirms an oshb: ref accompanies the original-language claim; collate.py returns byte tier for the added quote.

rulings.challenge_claim: The rejected_alternative rests on two Hebrew-token claims -- no royal/pride vocabulary carries over from 16:18-19, and tov appears in both 16:19 and 16:20 in different syntactic slots -- advanced entirely in transliteration, with no Hebrew quoted and no oshb: citation.
rulings.grounds: Confirmed: boundary_evidence_refs = web:Prov.16.20, web:Prov.16.18, web:Prov.16.19 only, no oshb:. Independent byte read of Prov.16.18 (לִפְנֵי שֶׁ֥בֶר גָּא֑וֹן וְלִפְנֵ֥י כִ֝שָּׁל֗וֹן גֹּ֣בַהּ רֽוּחַ), Prov.16.19 (ט֣וֹב שְׁפַל ר֭וּחַ אֶת עניים עֲנָוִ֑ים מֵֽחַלֵּ֥ק שָׁ֝לָ֗ל אֶת גֵּאִֽים), and Prov.16.20 (מַשְׂכִּ֣יל עַל דָּ֭בָר יִמְצָא ט֑וֹב וּבוֹטֵ֖חַ בַּיהוָ֣ה אַשְׁרָֽיו) confirms both underlying claims true: neither רֽוּחַ/גָּא֑וֹן (16:18) nor ר֭וּחַ/גֵּאִֽים (16:19) recurs in 16:20; and tov appears in 16:19 as the opening comparative and in 16:20 as the object of the opening clause, distinct syntactic slots. Boundary correct; citation form deficient under the same binding quote-the-original-language rule.
rulings.remedy: Add oshb:Prov.16.18, oshb:Prov.16.19, oshb:Prov.16.20 to boundary_evidence_refs; splice the byte-tier ruach and pride-root forms (16:18-19) and both tov tokens (16:19/16:20) into rejected_alternative with slot labels, replacing the transliteration-only phrasing. Test: citation_sweep.py / check_refs_mirror.py confirms oshb: presence; collate.py returns byte tier for each spliced quote.

rulings.challenge_claim: The rejected_alternative (no specific token repeats between 16:23 and 16:24 beyond the general speech domain) and the non-adjacent echo claim to 15:30 are advanced entirely in transliteration, with no Hebrew quoted and no oshb: citation.
rulings.grounds: Confirmed: boundary_evidence_refs = web:Prov.16.24, web:Prov.15.30, web:Prov.16.23 only, no oshb:. Independent byte read of Prov.16.23 (לֵ֣ב חָ֭כָם יַשְׂכִּ֣יל פִּ֑יהוּ וְעַל שְׂ֝פָתָ֗יו יֹסִ֥יף לֶֽקַח) versus Prov.16.24 (צוּף דְּ֭בַשׁ אִמְרֵי נֹ֑עַם מָת֥וֹק לַ֝נֶּפֶשׁ וּמַרְפֵּ֥א לָעָֽצֶם) confirms no shared root beyond the general speech domain (the mouth/lip root differs from the sayings root); Prov.15.30 (מְֽאוֹר עֵ֭ינַיִם יְשַׂמַּֽח לֵ֑ב שְׁמוּעָ֥ה ט֝וֹבָ֗ה תְּדַשֶּׁן עָֽצֶם) shares only the bone root (עָֽצֶם / לָעָֽצֶם) with 16:24, with a different governing verb ('fatten' vs 'heal'). Both claims true; citation form deficient under the same binding rule.
rulings.remedy: Add oshb:Prov.16.23, oshb:Prov.16.24, oshb:Prov.15.30 to boundary_evidence_refs; splice the byte-tier bone-root forms from both 15:30 and 16:24, plus the differing verbs, into rationale/device_notes. Test: same as above.

rulings.grounds: Confirmed: boundary_evidence_refs = web:Prov.16.33, web:Prov.16.1, web:Prov.16.10, web:Prov.16.11, web:Prov.16.32 only, no oshb:. Independent byte extraction (own splice, not copied from either packet) confirms Prov.16.1 token 4 and Prov.16.33 token 5 are byte-identical: וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה (16:1) and וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה (16:33) -- identical codepoints including cantillation, matching OL's claim exactly and confirming this is a stronger match (exact-phrase identity) than the row's 'same note it opened on' framing conveys. Boundary correct; citation form deficient under the same binding rule.
rulings.remedy: Add oshb:Prov.16.1 and oshb:Prov.16.33 to boundary_evidence_refs (and oshb:Prov.16.32, oshb:Prov.16.10-11 for the row's other two Hebrew-token claims); splice the byte-tier shared token into device_notes, upgrading the inclusio description from a general 'same note' gloss to the exact-phrase match it byte-verifies as. Test: same as above.
